0.long_answer: Mowat–Wilson syndrome is a genetic condition that causes a variety of developmental anomalies including distinctive facial features, intellectual disability, and multiple congenital anomalies. One of the key neurological features in individuals with Mowat–Wilson syndrome is the presence of recurrent seizures. These seizures are part of the clinical picture of epilepsy, which is characterized by repeated and unprovoked seizures due to abnormal electrical activity in the brain. Thus, epilepsy is a common neurological disorder in Mowat–Wilson syndrome.
